meta.title: My Family Research
meta.notes: Working family research file. Keep confirmed facts, leads, conflicts, and family stories separate.

project.name: My Family Research
project.privacy: Private family research. Do not publish living-person details without explicit permission.
project.goal: Turn the known family story into a sourced family tree with reviewable evidence.
project.seedStory: Replace this with what the family already knows: names, surnames, approximate dates, places, relationships, stories, photos/documents available, and biggest questions.
howToUseThisFile: The user downloads this template and fills in as much as they know.
AI agents edit this same JSON over time. Keep it valid JSON.
The user loads the updated file in JMO Ancestry with the Load data button.
Agents should add claims and researchTasks before rewriting person facts.
Promote a claim into a person profile only after sources support it.
agentInstructions: Preserve privacy. Do not add sensitive living-person details unless the user supplied them for private use.
Separate confirmed facts from leads, conflicts, and family lore.
Attach citations to every claim, event, relationship, and promoted fact.
Prefer direct records for parent-child links: birth records, census households, obituaries naming parents, probate, marriage records, or death certificates.
Do not merge same-name records without corroborating dates, relationships, geography, or source context.
Use normalized place records and reference them with placeId on birth, death, burial, and events.
When evidence conflicts, add a claim with status conflict and explain what blocks the merge.
Keep researchTasks current with the next concrete source or archive to search.
researchWorkflow: 1. Normalize known names, aliases, dates, places, and relationships into people.
2. Add places with coordinates for any known birth, residence, death, burial, census, immigration, military, or marriage events.
3. Create claims for all sourced facts and plausible leads.
4. Mark claim status as confirmed, needs-review, lead, or conflict.
5. Add researchTasks for open questions and unresolved links.
6. Update meta.updated whenever agents materially change the file.
7. Return the edited JSON file to the user so they can load it in the app.
